rationale: The candidate reads as a single, coherent stepped mass across all four views, so it has decent gesture clarity and repair integrity. The dominant form is legible and not overly fragmented, and the stepped silhouette is internally consistent. However, the program contract for neighborhood living requires an active ground threshold and one clear public void or terrace. Here the blue access edge is answered only weakly: the mass largely remains sealed, with no convincing carved court, undercut, or entry seam visible in the views. The result is more of a generic stepped object than a ground-active neighborhood building. The section also does not yet express a strong public/void hierarchy or an access-oriented sectional response. The form resonates somewhat with stepped precedent language, but it is still closer to an abstract pyramidal stack than to a socially active mixed neighborhood mass.
